conventions.convention: Symbols are ±1, indexed by all integers; S(s)_k=s_{k+1}. The relabelling φ(s)_k=(s_k+1)/2 pulls back the binary metric, with weights 2^{-(k+1)} multiplying sign differences in each defining one-sided series.
The unperturbed parameter satisfies a≥100, R=√a+3 and L=√(a−2R). B_R uses the supremum norm; h(s)=(x_{−1}(s),x_0(s)).
Sequential compactness is choice-free; the stated coding-homeomorphism and chaos conclusions assume AC_ω, while compactness is stated under AC_ω+DC.

Unstable slopes are u/v and stable slopes are v/u. D(F⁻¹)(x,y) is distinguished from [DF(x,y)]⁻¹; backward line invariance evaluates D(F⁻¹) at z_{n+1}. Homoclinic points exclude the fixed point, and transversality requires injective C¹ curves with nonzero independent tangents.
Cone invariance requires k(2L−k)≥1 in addition to 0<k<1 and L≥2.
The weighted norm is sup_{n≥0} θ^{−n}|u_n|, with 0<θ<1 and q=c(θ+θ⁻¹)<1. Update maps have C² extensions to an open neighborhood of J×J, and reference coordinates have a uniform interior margin.

Perturbed coding uses first coordinates q_n and phase points (q_n,V(q_n,q_{n+1})), with l=√a−3. Both G and the distinct map ΣG⁻¹Σ must satisfy the six bounds on [−R−1,R+1]², with 0<ε≤1/6 and C(a,R)ε≤1.

The oscillator is dimensionless, ω=dq∧dp and ι_{X_H}ω=dH. Its nonnegative normalized pulse repeats with period P=π/2+δ; G_δ=K_δ∘R_0 is defined only where the maximal solution exists through one period. δ=0 is a rescaled comparison equation, not a member of the original pulse family.

load_bearing.statement: For a≥100, R=√a+3 and L=√(a−2R), T_s maps B_R into itself and satisfies ‖T_sx−T_sy‖∞≤L⁻¹‖x−y‖∞. Each code has exactly one fixed point x(s), with sign x_n(s)=s_n, |x_n(s)|≥L and x_{n+1}(s)+x_{n−1}(s)=x_n(s)²−a.

Under the stated compact-interval, C²-extension, derivative, reference-orbit and margin hypotheses, T_b contracts the complete weighted ball with constant q=c(θ+θ⁻¹)<1. Its unique fixed point u(b) is C¹, satisfies ‖u(b)‖θ≤c|b−b_*|/(1−q), and has derivative norm at most c/(1−q).

For the stated C² map and inverse branch, ‖e‖C¹≤C(a,R)ε. When η=Cε≤1, each sign has exactly one root M_s(u,w) in its window, with both margins ≥3/4 and |∂_uM_s|,|∂_wM_s|≤(1+η)/(2l−η)≤2/13. P_{u,w}(v)=0 iff B(u,V(u,v))=V(v,w).

Under the stated forward and conjugated-inverse bounds, G has a uniquely coded invariant set, a coding homeomorphism under AC_ω, compactness under AC_ω+DC, chaos under AC_ω with sensitivity constant 2l, two hyperbolic coded fixed points, and transverse homoclinic points for every nonconstant code equal to one sign on both sufficiently distant tails.

For sufficiently small positive δ, the pulse solutions from S exist throughout [0,1] in the stated compact tube; K_δ→K and G_δ→F in C¹ with O(δ) bounds. G_δ is a smooth symplectic diffeomorphism on a neighborhood of S, and ΣG_δ⁻¹Σ is defined near S and is likewise C¹-close to F.

For every nonempty set S, bounded real functions on S are complete in the supremum metric, as is B_R(S) for every R≥0. D_± is a metric and φ is a bijective isometry onto the binary shift space; bilateral and one-sided bounded sequence spaces inherit completeness.

Grant AC_ω and DC. For fixed a≥100 and normalized pulse w, there is δ_0>0 such that every 0<δ<δ_0 gives a compact coded invariant set for G_δ conjugate to the two-sign shift, chaotic in the stated sense, with two hyperbolic coded fixed points and transverse homoclinic points for every nonconstant finite-deviation code.

concerns.concern: The Example says 'the pulse is supported in (π/2,P)', and Verification 3.1 says 'β_δ vanishes outside [π/2,P]'. The defined β_δ is a nonzero P-periodic function on all of R. Since its integral over a period is 1, it is positive somewhere in the first pulse interval and at that point translated by every integer multiple of P. The support assertion needs an explicit restriction to the first period; as written it is false globally.

Proof 2.2 starts 'fix b and put z*_k:=y_k+u_k(b)' before Proof 3.1 establishes the existence of u(b). Its derivative bound also says 'taking the fixed point of the homogeneous contraction started at 0', although the nonzero derivative is the fixed point of the affine, forced map. The ball-invariance and Banach argument closes the existence issue immediately, and the affine fixed-point equation gives the bound; the proof order and homogeneous/affine wording should reflect those arguments.

Proof 6.1 concludes 'By [[thm-higher-regularity-of-local-inverses]], K_δ has smooth local inverses'. That supplier states regularity of 'every local inverse supplied by the inverse function theorem'; it does not itself construct one. The inverse-function existence step should be identified explicitly before applying higher regularity. The declared Newton-contraction supplier provides an immediate route, so this is a short citation/inference gap rather than a defect in the endpoint-map claim.

The final paragraph says the unperturbed quadratic 'has endpoint values −25 and 43 at v=7 and v=13'. The example actually proves uniform inequalities: 49−100−u−w≤−25 and 169−100−u−w≥43 for u,w∈[−13,13]. These are worst-case endpoint bounds, not the endpoint values for arbitrary parameters; for u=w=0 the values are −51 and 69.

The Definition labels its correspondence 'with the published two-symbol space', and the Remarks repeatedly call its suppliers published. The actual files def-cm-bilateral-shift-space-and-cylinders and lem-cm-bilateral-shift-metric-and-sequential-compactness currently have status: draft. Their mathematical content is available, but the stated publication status is inaccurate.

alerts.finding: The physical_scope says 'the fixed points are 1 plus or minus sqrt(101)', and the title likewise lists these as 'the fixed points' of the pulsed horseshoe. The Example body correctly specifies 'the fixed points of the limiting quadratic map'. For positive δ, the supplier thm-explicit-perturbed-horseshoe-and-transversality instead defines the fixed points through ρ_u=M_u(ρ_u,ρ_u) and phase coordinates (ρ_u,V(ρ_u,ρ_u)); it gives no equality with the unperturbed surds. Carry the body's limiting-map qualification into the title and physical_scope.

seams_checked.note: The oscillator uses the supplier's dq∧dp and ι_Xω=dH conventions, giving q'=H_p and p'=−H_q. Time-dependent symplecticity is proved locally rather than inferred from an autonomous-only statement.

Binary metric weights, cylinder bounds, shift direction and the four-part chaos definition are preserved. The owned compactness claims retain AC_ω+DC, and homeomorphism claims retain AC_ω. Publication labels are inaccurate as recorded in concerns, but the cited propositions are used faithfully.

The stroboscopic map is defined through maximal solutions existing through one period. The oscillator definition explicitly identifies its endpoint-map domain with that supplier's domain and does not assume global completeness.

Pulse continuation uses compact time-state tubes inside the open ODE domain. The backward argument applies the same criterion to a time-reflected field; bounded state values alone are not substituted for compact trapping.
The single-flip example uses the exact shift direction and chaos vocabulary. Its nonperiodicity and two-sided convergence claims require only coding injectivity and the finite-word lemma.

The physical theorem retains a≥100, the pulse-width threshold, AC_ω+DC and local map domains. Its dimensional rescaling is explicit; full six-dimensional hyperbolicity and transversality are separately derived using the adopted transverse inverted oscillators. Perturbed momentum bounds correctly use V and the root margins.

The detailed example distinguishes the limiting quadratic constants from positive-width pulse bounds, but its title and physical_scope omit the limiting qualification for 1±√101. This overstatement is routed in alerts. Its arithmetic, units and physical coded-state bounds otherwise match the suppliers.
